title: Don’t Expect Fireworks From the Trump-Xi Summit
gist: China Brief: Palmer expects no breakthroughs from the Trump-Xi Washington summit because both sides are constrained (Trump weak at home and chastened by China's critical-mineral squeeze; China reeling from its property crisis); trade, minerals and AI top the agenda, with Taiwan a risk of a Trump verbal slip. Also: PLA purges leave the military unfit for near-term campaigns, and the U.S. is gutting its own China-studies institutions.

insights.claim: Neither side is positioned for anything dramatic at the Trump-Xi summit: Trump is weak at home and chastened by Beijing's critical-mineral export squeeze, while China is still reeling from its property crisis.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.so_what: Base case is status quo in U.S.-China trade; limited summit-driven market moves.
insights.quote: More fundamentally, neither side is in a position to try anything dramatic.

insights.claim: Top summit priorities are likely managing trade and securing supply of Chinese critical minerals.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.so_what: Critical-mineral supply remains China's key leverage over the U.S.
insights.locator: Xi’s task is simply to signal

insights.claim: The U.S. almost seized a Chinese ship last week based on a mistaken intelligence report produced with AI.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.so_what: AI-driven intelligence errors are a new escalation risk in U.S.-China relations.
insights.quote: the United States almost seized a Chinese ship last week based on a mistaken intelligence report produced with AI

insights.claim: U.S.-China AI safety agreement is unlikely because the U.S. industry favors alignment-based frameworks while China favors holding companies and executives directly liable, an approach anathema to Silicon Valley.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.so_what: Divergent AI liability regimes complicate global standards for AI firms.
insights.quote: China favors an approach that is anathema to Silicon Valley: holding companies and executives directly responsible for what they create

insights.claim: The Iran war is unlikely to be on the agenda: Trump has pulled back from confronting China over its alleged support for Iran, and Xi is again skipping UNGA in person.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.so_what: Reduces risk of U.S. secondary sanctions on China over Iran near-term.
insights.locator: I don’t expect the Iran war

insights.claim: Xi will likely press Trump on Taiwan, and Trump may abandon careful ambiguity and say something he shouldn't, triggering panic in Taiwan over U.S. abandonment.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.so_what: Headline risk for Taiwan assets and regional defense names post-summit.
insights.quote: I would not be surprised if, coming out of the summit, Trump parrots the language of the last impressive person he spoke to

insights.claim: Taiwan's reliance on U.S. protection has often kept it from taking its own defense seriously.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.so_what: Abandonment fears could spur Taiwanese defense reform and spending.

insights.claim: The 2027 Taiwan-invasion deadline is less commonly cited in U.S. discourse, possibly because about 83 percent of China experts surveyed in 2022 disagreed with it.
insights.speaker: James Palmer

insights.claim: Xi's military purges have left the PLA unfit for any serious near-term campaign; Gens. Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli were formally expelled, with political disobedience listed before corruption.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.quote: Xi has carved holes into the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) leadership, leaving the military unfit for any serious campaign in the near term.

insights.claim: The U.S. military is eliminating civilian positions at the Air Force's China Aerospace Studies Institute, following last year's gutting of civilian China-studies infrastructure.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.so_what: Degrades U.S. analytic capacity on its main rival.

insights.claim: Alibaba's Xianyu marketplace faces likely regulatory punishment after a TV investigation found coded sex-work ads, not its first such incident.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.so_what: Regulatory risk for Alibaba's secondhand marketplace.
insights.quote: Xianyu has apologized but is likely to face regulatory punishment
